title: Database Migration Timeline
purpose: Show the chronological sequence of SQL migrations run against Supabase PostgreSQL, grouped by feature area, with post-launch patches distinguished from original migrations.
audience: Database administrators, backend developers, DevOps engineers, project managers
description: Gantt chart presenting the chronological sequence of over 15 SQL migrations grouped by feature area: Foundation (create_profiles_and_auth, create_content_table), Payments (create_transactions, create_subscriptions, add_platform_fee_fields), Messaging (create_messages_conversations, add_voice_message_support), Analytics (create_analytics_events, create_analytics_summary), Admin and Settings (create_platform_settings, create_support_tickets), Content (create_content_related, update_content_schema — critical post-launch patch), Engagement (create_contests, update_contests_schema — critical post-launch patch, create_referrals), Premium (create_enclave_table). The two critical-path patches (update_content_schema, update_contests_schema) are flagged as post-launch fixes, indicating schema instability in core domains.
preconditions: Supabase PostgreSQL database has been provisioned
Migration scripts are versioned and stored in migrations/ directory
postconditions: All 17 migration scripts have been applied sequentially
Database schema reflects all feature areas with proper tables, indexes, and constraints

errorPaths.recovery: Manual rollback and fix before re-running

validationRules: Migrations must be applied in chronological order
Each migration must be idempotent or tracked in migration history
Post-launch patches (update_content_schema, update_contests_schema) require careful back-compat
securityConsiderations: Platform settings table stores sensitive configuration values
Profile and auth tables contain PII — migration changes must preserve data privacy
Blockchain tx hash in transactions table is application-enforced unique
performanceConsiderations: Index creation should be done as separate migrations to avoid table locks
Large table migrations (transactions, analytics_events) may require batching
annotations: update_content_schema.sql and update_contests_schema.sql are post-launch critical patches
Foundation + Payments + Messaging make up the first half of the migration timeline
Premium/Enclave is the last feature area migrated
